values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A Reuters report from July 2023, printed in Pipeline and Gas Journal, says a fire shut part of a Columbia Gas Transmission line in Virginia. That cut gas to Cove Point, which the report calls an LNG export plant, and the Loudoun LNG interconnect on that line went to near zero.

verifications.note: Reuters report reprinted in Pipeline and Gas Journal, July 26, 2023: a fire on Columbia Gas Transmission in Virginia cut gas to Cove Point via the Loudoun LNG interconnect; Cove Point called an LNG export plant.

records.researcher_notes: Single 2023 news report. The row is the system-wide Columbia Gas Transmission row, and the tie is to a Virginia line feeding Cove Point, so it is tagged as medium. The Cove Point terminal is listed as export and import; the report calls it an export plant. No existing values on the sheet were changed.

ledger.note: A search for Colorado Interstate Gas and LNG export found no source tying this system to an LNG terminal. The EIA text and the existing refs cover only the pipeline's capacity and history.
The EIA entries and the Federal Register notice describe a Raton Basin lateral serving Colorado markets. Searches found no source tying it to LNG exports.
The EIA entry and the Federal Register notice describe a 2002 Raton Basin expansion. No source found ties it to LNG exports.
The EIA entry and the NGI news report on the 2005 FERC certificate describe a Raton Basin looping project. The report names no LNG tie.
The EIA entry and the 2000 Federal Register notice describe a Raton Basin expansion. No source found ties it to LNG exports.
The EIA entries and the 2001 Federal Register notice describe the Valley Line expansion in Colorado. The notice names no LNG tie.
The Federal Register notice and EIA entry describe a 41-mile Colorado lateral serving the Greeley market. No LNG tie appears in the text.
The TC Energy releases describe the Appalachia Supply Project as a power and industrial growth expansion for the Columbia system. A search found no LNG tie.
The Federal Register notice and EIA entries describe the East Side expansion serving Pennsylvania, New York, and New Jersey markets. No source found ties it to LNG exports.
The EIA entry and the 2005 Federal Register notice describe the Hardy Storage loops in Virginia. The text names no LNG tie.
The 2005 Federal Register notice and EIA entry describe the Line 1278 replacement in Pennsylvania. The text names no LNG tie.
The 2013 Federal Register notice and EIA entry describe the Line MB extension in Maryland. A search found no source tying it to Cove Point or any export terminal.
The EIA entry and the cited Chinese filing describe a cancelled 0.5-mile Kentucky replacement. No LNG tie appears in the sources.
The TC Energy fact sheet, FERC notice, and EIA entry describe a reliability replacement in Kentucky and Ohio. The text names no LNG tie.
The Ohio Power Siting Board and EIA entries describe a distribution loop north and west of Columbus, Ohio. No source ties it to LNG.

A Reuters report in Pipeline and Gas Journal from July 2023 says Cove Point, which it calls an LNG export plant, got gas from Columbia Gas's Loudoun LNG interconnect on a Columbia Virginia line. The tie is to that Virginia line, and the system-wide row is tagged on that basis.
The EIA entry and the 2022 Federal Register notices describe compressor work to serve Virginia and Hampton Roads markets. The text names no LNG export tie.
A search for the Virginia Reliability Project and Cove Point found no link. The project serves the Hampton Roads and Chesapeake market.

Sources tie the Columbia Gulf expansions to LNG (the Louisiana XPress to Sabine Pass and the East Lateral XPress to Plaquemines). The tie belongs to those expansion rows, not to the mainline itself, so this mainline row stays blank.
A search found no source tying the Maysville project to LNG. Its stated purpose is gas for a Kentucky power plant.
